help.InterfaceSettings.title: {ui.interface}
help.InterfaceSettings.feature1.title: {ui.style}
help.InterfaceSettings.feature1.body:
The styles list in Resources/Schema configures display names and resource paths, such as Style/YourStyle. Display names come directly from each entry's Name field in Schema and do not change with the UI language. All style resources reside under Resources/Style.

Selecting a style prepares its resources asynchronously, then replaces the appearance in place and saves the selection. Windows and controls are not rebuilt; drafts, input and scroll positions are preserved.

Style, font and language share a loading lock. Failed selections fall back in Schema order; the current interface is kept only if every candidate fails. The Editor index preserves manual names and order and only appends newly discovered complete packages.

The first valid entry in Schema is the default style. Missing or unregistered saved selections use it. Unavailable resources are tried only in list order. No fixed style is added; an error is reported if none can be loaded. Reordering does not override a valid saved selection.

Deleted, missing or unloadable selections fall back to the first loadable entry in Schema order, and the applied selection is saved. Styles validate all page and control templates. If no candidate is usable, report an error and retain the running interface or language without committing a partial switch.
help.InterfaceSettings.feature2.title: {ui.font}
help.InterfaceSettings.feature2.body:
The fonts list in Schema configures fonts for all DevTools styles and overlays. Font display names come directly from each entry's Name field in Schema and are not localized. Included choices are Micro Hei Mono, Droid Sans CJK and Fusion Pixel 12px. Each file is below 5 MB.

Selection loads asynchronously, then applies and saves immediately. Micro Hei has monospaced Latin and full-width CJK, without a strict 2:1 cell ratio. The Droid choice uses proportional Latin.

The pixel font retains its source BMP characters and existing emoji, excluding rare supplementary glyphs. A lightweight Droid fallback fills ordinary gaps. These are not complete Unicode or color-emoji fonts.

Store fonts under Resources/Font and omit file extensions from paths. Changing language does not change the font. Previous large-font selections fall back to the current default. The game TMP font is unchanged.

The first valid entry in the Schema font list is the default. Missing or unregistered selections use it; unavailable resources are tried in list order, without adding a fixed font. An error is reported if none can be loaded. Valid saved selections take priority.

Deleted, missing or unloadable selections fall back to the first loadable entry in Schema order, and the applied selection is saved. Styles validate all page and control templates. If no candidate is usable, report an error and retain the running interface or language without committing a partial switch.
help.InterfaceSettings.feature3.title: Overall opacity
help.InterfaceSettings.feature3.body:
Overall opacity applies to the main window, external tabs, details, buttons, text, icons, scrollbars, badge, settings and help overlays. {ui.searchHistory} and context menus use the same value.

The slider uses a {Config_MIN_OPACITY}–{Config_MAX_OPACITY} scale and defaults to {Config_DEFAULT_PANEL_OPACITY}. Its minimum is {Config_MIN_PANEL_OPACITY}. Changes preview immediately and save automatically after {Config_CONFIG_SAVE_DELAY} seconds without further changes. Closing the tool also commits pending changes.

Text follows overall opacity with a minimum of {Config_MIN_TEXT_OPACITY}. Backgrounds, borders, images and scrollbars retain the normal overall opacity. Glyph edges and explicitly hidden editor text preserve their behavior. Floating logs have independent opacity settings.
help.InterfaceSettings.feature4.title: Independent floating logs
help.InterfaceSettings.feature4.body:
Floating logs have separate background and text opacity, without multiplication by overall opacity. Their background palette follows the current UI style without overwriting saved opacity.

Each style gives the badge its own outline and decoration. The badge and its settings still follow overall opacity. Dragging, click-to-restore, right-click settings and edge docking behave consistently.

Minimizing, restoring and reopening preserve the current settings. Saved values are loaded on restart.
help.Window.title: {ui.window}
help.Window.feature1.title: Help navigation
help.Window.feature1.body:
The help tree groups topics under Overview, {ui.console}, {ui.cheat}, {ui.macro} and {ui.options}. Click an arrow or group title to expand or collapse it; click a feature to read its content.

Long content is split into pages automatically. Use Previous, Next or the left and right arrow keys. Body text supports selection and copying. Navigation highlights the current feature as pages change.

Drag the help title bar to move the window. Clicking any {icon.help} opens the relevant topic at its first page and returns the help window to the center of the viewport.

Close with the close button, Esc or a click outside the window. Logs and running macros continue while help is open.
help.Window.feature2.title: Open, minimize and close
help.Window.feature2.body:
Press {ToolKey} to open the closed tool or restore it from the {ui.floating}. Pressing it in the open main window closes the tool by default. Enable “Minimize with shortcut when open” in {ui.options} / Settings to minimize instead.

Clicking the badge also restores it. The title bar {icon.minimize} minimizes; {icon.close} closes the tool and hides both the window and badge. The toggle key can reopen it.

Minimizing, closing and restoring preserve the current tab, position and size. Logging and running macros continue.
help.Window.feature3.title: Move and reset position
help.Window.feature3.body:
Drag the title bar to move the window, including beyond any viewport edge. External tabs and details follow the window.

Double-click the title bar to reset the position while keeping the current size. Title bar buttons do not trigger this reset.
help.Window.feature4.title: Resize and minimize
help.Window.feature4.body:
Drag the bottom-right corner to resize; release to commit. Width and height are each limited to 25–100% of the corresponding viewport dimension.

Click {icon.minimize} to minimize to the badge. The badge stays inside the viewport and docks when released near an edge.

Position and size are retained only for the current run and are not written to configuration.
help.Console.title: {ui.console}
help.Console.feature1.title: Input and completion
help.Console.feature1.body:
Enter {ui.console} commands in the bottom input field. Enter completes a suggestion or executes the current input. The up and down arrows navigate history or suggestions.

Ctrl+C focuses the {ui.console} input field; selecting stack trace text preserves native copying. Esc releases input focus.

Submitted commands, execution results and tool exceptions are classified as Dev, retaining their colors and actual stack traces.
help.Console.feature2.title: Combined filters
help.Console.feature2.body:
The Dev, Log, Warning and Error buttons independently control which types are displayed. Combine them freely.

Only the Unity log reception path maps to Log, Warning and Error. Unity Exception and Assert belong to Error. Tool Print output, command results, tool exceptions and macro messages belong to Dev. Debug.Log inside a command still belongs to Unity logs.

Select all types to show everything, or deselect all to show nothing.

Filtering affects only {ui.console}, not the latest-log previews in {ui.cheat} or the {ui.floating}.
help.Console.feature3.title: Icons and timestamps
help.Console.feature3.body:
The three independent toolbar toggles are {icon.type} Icons, {icon.timestamp} Timestamps and {icon.fold} Collapse. An active background indicates enabled; hover for details.

Icons show the log type using the same Emoji as the filter buttons.

Timestamps show or hide log receipt times immediately for cached and new logs. These settings change only {ui.console} presentation, without modifying raw bodies, filters or grouping, and are saved to configuration.

Unity engine logs are received by default; no additional switch is needed.
help.Console.feature4.title: Collapse
help.Console.feature4.body:
When enabled, only logs that are consecutive in the original reception order and have identical bodies and stack traces are merged. Time and type are not compared for equality.

Each entry shows its occurrence count and the latest time matching the current filters. Different intervening content starts a new group.

Disable collapsing to see each original record again; cached logs are not lost.
help.Console.feature5.title: History and new logs
help.Console.feature5.body:
After initialization, the tool caches all logs received during the current run. Reception continues while hidden, on other tabs or minimized.

Entering {ui.console} or changing filters starts with up to the latest {Config_CONSOLE_RECENT_LOG_COUNT} entries, preparing older entries upward from the newest. The newest log stays at the bottom; unused space remains above a short list. Adding older entries does not move existing text.

Scroll upward near the top to load earlier history outside that range. Scrollbar size may change as text heights become known.

New logs received while reading history show a notice. Click it to return to the latest range and resume following output.
help.Console.feature6.title: Counts and clearing
help.Console.feature6.body:
The received count is the raw number of logs received since the last clear, independent of filters and collapsing.

Click a log to select it and update its stack trace without automatically opening the sidebar. Use the arrow at the right edge to show or hide it.

Clear output deletes the cached logs, groups, selection and counts. These cannot be recovered in the tool.
help.Stack.title: {ui.stack}
help.Stack.feature1.title: Stack entries
help.Stack.feature1.body:
Adjacent stack entries use alternating backgrounds. A single click highlights only that entry; it does not jump to code or perform other actions.

Long entries wrap automatically. Blank lines remain as spacing. Selecting another log clears the highlight and returns to the top.
help.Stack.feature2.title: Select, copy and scroll
help.Stack.feature2.body:
Drag to select text within an entry and use the system copy shortcut. Text selection does not trigger an entry click.

Copy stack trace copies the entire original stack trace, without metadata or placeholder messages.

Browse long stacks with the mouse wheel, right scrollbar thumb or track. Unrelated incoming logs do not reset your reading position.
help.Stack.feature3.title: Missing stacks and input records
help.Stack.feature3.body:
When no actual stack trace exists, the sidebar displays "No stack trace provided for this log" and disables copying.

User-submitted command echoes in Dev display "User input". Other Dev output retains the actual stack trace provided instead of replacing it with that message.

The sidebar has a fixed width and overlays the log area in narrow windows. Hiding it preserves selection during the current run.
help.CheatCommands.title: {ui.cheatCommands}
help.CheatCommands.feature1.title: Search and categories
help.CheatCommands.feature1.body:
Category and search filters work together. Search matches command names, aliases, tags and descriptions using case-insensitive containment of the complete search term.

{icon.log} beside the search field opens history. Enter or leaving the field records the complete term. Commands, presets and macro grids share one history, while each searches its own data. No recommendations are added and result ordering is preserved.

Commands load progressively in order. Click one to display its form or presets on the right; hover for external details.
help.CheatCommands.feature2.title: Fixed macro entry
help.CheatCommands.feature2.body:
{ui.customMacros} stays at the top of the command list and cannot be unpinned or dragged.

Click it to display all available macros, including developer-defined built-ins using MacroAttribute and {ui.customMacros} saved in game.
help.CheatCommands.feature3.title: Context menu and pin order
help.CheatCommands.feature3.body:
Right-click a command to pin, unpin or copy a parameter-name template. Parameter aliases take precedence in the copied template.

New pins are appended to the pinned region. Drag a pinned handle to reorder and release to save. Items can move only within their own pinned region.

Unpinned commands sort by name. Pin state and order are saved to configuration.
help.CheatParameters.title: {ui.commandParameters}
help.CheatParameters.feature1.title: Fill and execute
help.CheatParameters.feature1.body:
After selecting a command, fill the form on the right in parameter declaration order. Names, types and defaults come from the existing command system.

Use {ui.console} parameter syntax and put text containing spaces in double quotes. Click Execute command to submit the form.

Help only explains the controls; it does not fill parameters or execute commands.
help.CheatPresets.title: {ui.presets}
help.CheatPresets.feature1.title: Find and execute presets
help.CheatPresets.feature1.body:
Presets are provided by developers. Search matches names, parameters and tags, excluding descriptions. {icon.log} opens shared history. Filtering affects only presets for the selected command.

The size slider changes button presentation; Previous and Next browse results.

Hover for details. Clicking a preset immediately submits its complete command.
help.CheatPresets.feature2.title: Jump to a page
help.CheatPresets.feature2.body:
Previous, page information and Next are centered. Previous on the first page wraps to the last; Next on the last page wraps to the first.

Enter a target page on the right and click Go. Out-of-range numbers are constrained to valid pages.

The target defaults to the following page, or page 1 from the last page. In narrow windows the jump controls move to a second row on the right to avoid covering the pager.
help.CheatPresets.feature3.title: Copy a preset
help.CheatPresets.feature3.body:
Right-click a preset and choose Copy to obtain exactly the complete command that would be sent to {ui.console}.

Preset context menus do not offer pinning.
help.CheatMacros.title: {ui.macroGrid}
help.CheatMacros.feature1.title: Find and run macros
help.CheatMacros.feature1.body:
Search matches macro names, descriptions and complete bodies, ignoring case. {icon.log} opens shared history. Selecting a term filters the current macro grid without executing a macro.

Use the size slider and paging buttons to browse.

Hover for details; click to run. Only one macro runs at a time. Stop prevents subsequent steps from executing.

Execution uses a snapshot of the body taken at startup. Changing tabs or closing the main window does not stop it.
help.CheatMacros.feature2.title: Pin and copy macros
help.CheatMacros.feature2.body:
Right-click a macro to pin, unpin or copy its body.

Pinned macros come first. Drag handles to change their order and release to save. Unpinned macros sort by name.

Renaming a custom macro preserves its pin. Commands and macros maintain separate saved pin orders.
help.MacroLibrary.title: {ui.macroLibrary}
help.MacroLibrary.feature1.title: Custom and {ui.builtInMacros}
help.MacroLibrary.feature1.body:
{ui.customMacros} can be created, edited, deleted and saved. {ui.builtInMacros} are collected only from registered command methods marked with MacroAttribute.

Built-ins are read-only. Copy one to a custom macro to edit it. New and copied drafts are written to the macro file only when saved.
help.MacroLibrary.feature2.title: Drafts and unsaved markers
help.MacroLibrary.feature2.body:
An asterisk means the current content has not been saved. Restoring the last saved name, description and body removes the marker.

Switching macros preserves drafts for this session, including drafts with errors. Unsaved drafts are not written to disk when the run ends.
help.MacroEditor.title: {ui.macroEditor}
help.MacroEditor.feature1.title: Edit and format
help.MacroEditor.feature1.body:
Edit the name, description and command body separately. Use one command per line, aligned left without indentation. Custom bodies support up to {Config_MAX_MACRO_BODY_LINES} lines including blanks and comments. Longer drafts point to the first excess line and remain intact, but cannot be saved or run.

The editor always shows a vertical scrollbar and supports horizontal scrolling for long lines. Line numbers follow the native text scroll position.

Format removes leading indentation while preserving strings, blank lines and comment meaning. Cursor movement, selection, clipboard operations and undo use native text editing.
help.MacroEditor.feature2.title: Validate and save
help.MacroEditor.feature2.body:
The editor checks syntax, command existence, parameter counts and statically detectable type errors. Validation does not execute commands.

Error text and line numbers turn red. Click diagnostics to locate the first error. Saving and running are disabled while errors exist.

Saving updates the {ui.cheat} macro grid immediately. Built-ins cannot be overwritten.
help.MacroEditor.feature3.title: Run and stop
help.MacroEditor.feature3.body:
Execution uses a snapshot of the current body. Only one macro runs at a time. Switching tabs or closing the window does not stop it.

Stop prevents later lines from running; it does not forcibly terminate business async methods already started. Errors report the macro name, original line and cause.

Built-ins pass raw parameters to the existing command system. {ui.customMacros} use the macro language; their parsing rules are independent.
help.MacroSyntax.title: {ui.macroSyntax}
help.MacroSyntax.feature1.title: Keywords and examples
help.MacroSyntax.feature1.body:
Select a keyword to see its syntax, behavior, limits and examples without changing the editor body.

Strings use quotes. // outside a string begins a comment. {ui.customMacros} cannot call other macros.

In a narrow window, Syntax reference opens an overlay drawer. Click outside it or press Esc to close.
help.MacroSyntax.feature2.title: Loops
help.MacroSyntax.feature2.body:
Repeat accepts only integer literals from {Config_MIN_MACRO_REPEAT_COUNT} to {Config_MAX_MACRO_REPEAT_COUNT}. Nesting is not supported; multiple separate loops may appear in sequence.

Repeat({Config_MIN_MACRO_REPEAT_COUNT})
GetCoin(0, 100)
WaitFor(0.2)
EndRepeat()

Execution is continuous without waits and does not automatically yield frames.
help.MacroSyntax.feature3.title: Waiting
help.MacroSyntax.feature3.body:
WaitFor() waits until the next frame.

WaitFor(0.2) waits for that many seconds, independently of timeScale.

WaitFor(SomeAsyncCommand()) calls the command once and awaits completion. Task, UniTask, their generic forms and IEnumerator are supported. Synchronous methods complete on return. Ordinary calls do not wait for asynchronous results.
help.MacroSyntax.feature4.title: Syntax colors and widths
help.MacroSyntax.feature4.body:
After selecting a wait or loop keyword, choose a preset color or restore the default. Repeat and EndRepeat share a color. Error red is fixed and takes precedence.

Both color groups are saved to configuration. The {ui.macroLibrary} is fixed at 180 panel units and the syntax sidebar at 240, without resize handles. Narrow windows use a syntax overlay drawer.
help.ConsoleSettings.title: {ui.console}
help.ConsoleSettings.feature1.title: Preload and display
help.ConsoleSettings.feature1.body:
Entering {ui.console} or changing filters starts with at most the latest {Config_CONSOLE_RECENT_LOG_COUNT} logs. This count is fixed. Earlier history remains cached and loads on demand when scrolling up.

Show log type icons, Show log timestamps and Collapse identical logs share configuration with the {ui.console} toolbar and apply immediately. Leaving {ui.options} or closing the tool saves to the existing configuration file.
help.ConsoleSettings.feature2.title: Other {ui.console} settings
help.ConsoleSettings.feature2.body:
Input history capacity, query cache capacity, query limit, recording failed commands and exception stack settings apply the next time Play starts.

Unity engine logs are received by default.

Leaving {ui.options} or closing the tool commits pending settings.
help.CheatSettings.title: {ui.cheat}
help.CheatSettings.feature1.title: Latest log preview
help.CheatSettings.feature1.body:
Latest log lines ranges from {Config_MIN_CHEAT_LOG_COUNT} to {Config_MAX_CHEAT_LOG_COUNT}. Set 0 to hide the bottom {ui.cheat} preview; other values show up to that many lines.

This setting synchronizes immediately with the {ui.cheat} page slider and saves automatically. Floating log count is independent. {ui.console} caching and display are unaffected.
help.CheatSettings.feature2.title: {ui.searchHistory}
help.CheatSettings.feature2.body:
Commands, {ui.presets} and macro grids share one search and history implementation, but search independent data. No recommendations are provided and existing result order is retained.

{ui.searchHistory} capacity defaults to {Config_DEFAULT_CHEAT_SEARCH_HISTORY_CAPACITY}, with a minimum of {Config_MIN_CHEAT_SEARCH_HISTORY_CAPACITY} and maximum of {Config_MAX_CHEAT_SEARCH_HISTORY_CAPACITY}. Changes apply and save immediately; reducing capacity retains the newest entries. Case-insensitive duplicates move to the front; empty terms are ignored.

Click {icon.log} beside a search field to choose a term. Hover highlights an option. The dropdown shows up to {Config_SEARCH_HISTORY_VISIBLE_ITEMS} entries at once; use the wheel or scrollbar for more.

History is saved in configuration and is separate from {ui.console} command input history.
help.CheatSettings.feature3.title: Manage {ui.searchHistory}
help.CheatSettings.feature3.body:
The {ui.cheat} section in {ui.options} provides Clear history and View history below capacity.

Clear history deletes all shared search records. View history displays complete terms with scrolling, text selection and copying, plus a Delete button for each entry.

Clearing and deletion save immediately and preserve the relative order of remaining terms. They do not change search field text or execute any command in a term. Close with the button, Esc or a click outside.
help.FloatingSettings.title: {ui.floating}
help.FloatingSettings.feature1.title: Log preview
help.FloatingSettings.feature1.body:
Choose whether the badge shows latest logs and set the entry count from {Config_MIN_FLOATING_LOG_COUNT} to {Config_MAX_FLOATING_LOG_COUNT}.

This preview ignores {ui.console} filters and collapsing. The main window, badge, settings and help do not actively disable game input.
help.FloatingSettings.feature2.title: Opacity and saving
help.FloatingSettings.feature2.body:
Background and text opacity are independent. {Config_MAX_PERCENTAGE}% is fully visible; {Config_MIN_PERCENTAGE}% is transparent.

Changes apply and save automatically and synchronize with the floating settings in {ui.options}.

Closing help returns to the current settings panel. Esc closes only the topmost help window; press it again to close floating settings.
help.InterfaceSettings.feature5.title: Interface language
help.InterfaceSettings.feature5.body:
The languages list in Schema configures language codes, native names and directories. The first loadable entry is the default language and the fallback for missing translations. Each language has its own directory; Simplified Chinese is not inserted automatically.

ui.json contains interface text and icons, help.json contains help, and macro.json contains macro syntax references. Dynamic text uses named placeholders.

Missing or unregistered saved selections use the default language. Valid saved selections take priority. Selection loads asynchronously and commits atomically without rebuilding windows or changing drafts. Existing logs, actual stack traces and business names remain unchanged.

Deleted, missing or unloadable selections fall back to the first loadable entry in Schema order, and the applied selection is saved. Styles validate all page and control templates. If no candidate is usable, report an error and retain the running interface or language without committing a partial switch.
help.ToolSettings.title: {ui.settings}
help.ToolSettings.feature1.title: Toggle shortcut
help.ToolSettings.feature1.body:
The shortcut combines one optional modifier with one base key. Choose None, Ctrl, Alt or Shift. Left and right modifiers are equivalent; multiple modifiers cannot be combined.

Base keys include F1–F15, A–Z, top-row digits and punctuation. Space, arrows, Esc and numpad keys are excluded. Select physical keys; for example, Shift + 1 represents ! on the standard number row.

The held modifiers must match the selection exactly. Additional modifiers prevent activation. Changes apply and save immediately and persist after restart.
help.ToolSettings.feature2.title: Open, close and minimize
help.ToolSettings.feature2.body:
Press {ToolKey} to open the closed tool or restore it from the {ui.floating}.

“Minimize with shortcut when open” is off by default: pressing the shortcut in the open main window closes the tool. Enable it to minimize to the badge instead.

The title bar minimize and close buttons retain their individual actions. Tabs, position, size and draft input are preserved; logging and running macros continue.
